subject: Midterm volume rebalancing and commit design
messages:
From: Jordan Myers <jm@helixcare.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelixCare Procurement <procurement@helixcare.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Midterm capacity change / renewal sync

Hi Grace,

Quick note from procurement — we're seeing higher-than-expected usage in Q4 and need to lock additional capacity for the next 9 months while we finalize product changes. Current committed footprint: 200k tokens/month (annualized). Expected incremental need: +120k tokens/month immediately.

Can you outline the best ways to handle this mid-contract? Our procurement team prefers one of the following:
- Add a recurring committed uplift (amendment) that runs until our Jan 1 renewal and then co-terms/annualizes, or
- Take a one-time true-up/top-up with a credit structure to cover overages for the remainder of the contract.

Key constraints: PO required by Jan 22 to hit deployment schedule; legal will prefer a light amendment; finance needs clear invoice cadence (pro-rata vs billed upfront). Can you and your team send options + high-level cost math? I attached our internal worksheet.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Myers
Director, Platform Ops
HelixCare
Attachment: HELIX_USAGE_WORKSHEET_Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Myers <jm@helixcare.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity change / renewal sync

Jordan — thanks for the detail and the worksheet. Looping in Karthik (pricing/ops) and Marissa (AE) so we can move quickly. High-level response below; we can put formal math into an amendment once you pick a path. Attachment: HELIX_QTY_CHANGE_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub)

Options we recommend (short form):

Option 1 — Recurring uplift (Amendment):
- Add +120k tokens/month as a reserved committed block.
- Billing: monthly invoice; credit on overage if you stay within 110% of new commit.
- Pricing: incremental block priced at our committed tier rate; for visibility we can offer an 8% uplift discount off list for a 12-month term.
- Pros: Predictable unit economics, simpler month-to-month planning.

Option 2 — One-time true-up with credit (short-term bridge):
- One-time purchase to cover estimated incremental usage through Jan 1 renewal (pro-rated).
- Apply a credit for actuals at renewal; credit may be consumed against future consumption.
- Pricing: one-time incremental purchase with a 12% discount on the incremental units for the remaining contract months.
- Pros: Lowest near-term cash increase, minimal contractual changes.

Follow-ups / constraints we need from you:
- Confirm desired path (Amendment vs True-up) by Jan 18 to make PO timeline.
- If Amendment, confirm desired commitment length (we can offer improved banding for 18- or 24-month commits).
- Any internal billing/GL code for the invoice.

If it helps, Karthik can run a few price scenarios and draft an amendment for legal review. Thoughts?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: Jordan Myers <jm@helixcare.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelixCare Procurement <procurement@helixcare.io>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity change / renewal sync

Grace — thanks, that framing is helpful. Procurement preference is Option 2 (one-time true-up) unless we can get a deeper concession for a longer commit. Two follow-up asks: 

1) If we move to an 18-month uplift (i.e., +120k/month committed for 18 months), can Redwood do 10% off the incremental block? That gets us comfortable with the added spend.
2) If we stick with the true-up, can you confirm the exact pro-rata math and whether the credit can be applied to the first invoice after renewal (we want the accounting to be clean on our side).

We need to get an approved commercial path to procurement by Jan 22. If you can provide a doc (amendment draft or true-up SOW) + indicative invoice by Jan 18 we can get a PO to you.

On the pricing ask — if 10% is not standard, would there be a negotiated exception for committed 18 months? Also cc'ing our procurement lead for visibility.

—Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing math / 18-month concession option for HelixCare

Grace / Marissa — ran the numbers based on Jordan's ask. Below is a concise breakdown and recommended commercial concession we can offer without escalating to CRO: 

Assumptions: current commit = 200k tokens/mo; incremental = 120k tokens/mo; list price per token-block = $0.00012 (example rate), remaining term until Jan 1 renewal = 11 months.

Paths: 
A) 1x true-up (credit path) — remaining 11 months:
- Quantity covered: 120k * 11 = 1,320,000 tokens.
- List cost: 1,320,000 * $0.00012 = $158.40 (example unit math for demo; actual invoice will be in whole dollars).
- Discount: 12% -> effective cost ~$139.39 -> invoice as one-time line item/credit.

B) 18-month amendment (preferred by customer):
- Quantity covered: 120k * 18 = 2,160,000 tokens.
- List cost: 2,160,000 * $0.00012 = $259.20.
- Concession: we can approve 10% off incremental block for 18-month commit (one-time exception).
- Effective: ~$233.28; billed monthly across 18 months or as agreed.

Recommendation: Offer Option B (18-month commit at 10% off incremental block) as a commercial sweetener but require a signed amendment (Amendment_HELIX_2026_draft.docx). If HelixCare wants to minimize paperwork, offer the true-up with 12% and a fast-track amendment if they convert to a longer commit later.

Action items I can take: draft amendment, prepare DocuSign, and create an indicative invoice for procurement. Grace — please confirm we can approve 10% for this account.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Pricing & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Amendment_HELIX_2026_draft.docx (draft amendment stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Myers <jm@helixcare.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: amendment vs true-up + mutual action plan

Jordan — good thread. We can approve the 10% concession on the incremental block for an 18-month commitment as outlined by Karthik. To keep procurement on schedule, here are proposed next steps (mutual action plan):

1) HelixCare confirms path by end-of-day Jan 18 (Option A: 1x true-up at 12% or Option B: 18-month commit at 10%).
2) If Option B chosen, Redwood will: 
   - Send DocuSign amendment (Amendment_HELIX_2026_draft.docx) within 24 hours of confirmation.
   - Finance will prepare a monthly invoice schedule; first invoice pro-rated to amendment effective date if mid-month.
3) If Option A chosen, Redwood will: 
   - Issue one-time invoice for pro-rated incremental units with 12% discount; credit applied to first post-renewal invoice.
4) Legal: Marissa will route the amendment for a light redline; expected turn-around 48–72 hours.
5) Procurement: target PO submission by Jan 22 to meet deployment timeline.

I'll kick this off once you confirm which path you want to proceed with. Thanks everyone for moving quickly — cc'ing Aditya from sales ops so he has visibility on the ask.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
redwood.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0192
